done.why: I typed my 31st line (go southwest from the Deep Canyon) and the world told me I'd used all 30 turns the session allows. I wasn't done; I'd just started finding where the open paths were.

about: It's Zork with the map collapsed in on itself. Same white house, same mailbox, same troll behind the trap door, but once you're underground somebody has barred the door behind you, the Round Room's passages are caved in, the dam is boarded up 'for inspection', and a whole stretch is drowned under still black water. Someone has been down here before me, sorting rubble into neat piles by size. It feels like being locked into a shrinking cave with one other person in it who I never saw.

moments.note: The trap door crashed shut and I heard someone bar it. I expected it to slam; I did not expect a 'someone'.
Troll fight dragged on: six swings, got knocked to my knees, started wondering if I'd die on turn 18 of a 30-turn session.
Took the troll's head off and the body vanished in black fog. Felt earned.
Cave-in rubble sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, with grit still trickling. That one line did more for atmosphere than anything else.
'Bar bar ...' - the room echoed my words back and I had no idea what it wanted from me.
Saying 'echo' changed the acoustics and then the bar was mine. Small puzzle, solved fast, nice.
'FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' Made me laugh out loud.
Second blocked exit in a row; starting to feel like I'm being herded and running out of turns to find where to.
Turn cap hit mid-exploration with three exits still untried. I wanted ten more minutes.

wished: I wished I could tell who barred the trap door, or at least shout up at them. The game told me 'someone' and then never let me do anything about it.
I wished the Round Room told me which passages were caved in on arrival instead of making me burn a turn on each, with a 30-turn budget.
I wished I could have gone southwest or down from the Deep Canyon. The water sounds from below were the most interesting lead I had when I was cut off.
I wished combat were faster. Six swings at one troll is a fifth of my whole session.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: This is the moment the game told me it wasn't the one I half-remembered. 'Someone' means I'm not alone down here.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: Best line in the session. It implies a person, a habit, and a lot of time, without naming anything.

lines.line: FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.
lines.why: Funny, and it tells me the blocked paths are deliberate and in-world, not just missing.

lines.line: the floor goes down under black water lying perfectly still, and does not come up again anywhere your light can reach.
lines.why: Genuinely eerie. 'Perfectly still' did the work.

fun.why: The opening was brisk and I was underground with a sword by turn 13, which is exactly what an impatient player wants. The troll fight (turns 15-20) and the Loud Room (25-27) were good fun. But the back third was hitting walls, and the cap landed right as it got interesting.

engagement.why: I never considered quitting. The barred door at 13 and the sorted rubble at 23 hooked me, and the dam sign at 29 kept me. I stopped because the world stopped me.

difficulty.why: Nothing stumped me. The echo thing at 25-26 cost me one turn of confusion. The troll was more attrition than challenge. The hard part was the turn budget, not the puzzles.

interestingness.why: The idea of someone else working the caves ahead of me, barring doors and sorting rubble, is a strong hook and it was delivered in two or three sentences. The flooded northwest at 30 and the water below the canyon suggested there's a shape to what's been cut off. I wanted to know why.

prose.why: The new writing is noticeably better than the old boilerplate around it. 'Grit is still trickling from it as you watch', 'water that would rather not be disturbed', 'perfectly still' - compact and specific. The original room text is fine but flat by comparison.
